hypothesis: The compact-refine decompose's reported-only candidate #4 (record 20260928-070500, bench 61b1f3b): harness_digest_inputs runs at compact ENTER (11.9ms p50 at stock-10MiB, the enter->digest_captured span) while the digest renders only at the commit, and TS captures at the commit (_harnessDigestWithFingerprint immediately before appendCompaction) — deferring the capture to post-summarizer would shave the pre-LLM path. GATED by the parity check: does the capture placement change the CAPTURED CONTENT or the observable behavior? The lane's job: characterize both placements' captures, run the parity check class-by-class, and ship the byte-identity oracle over both placements (the placement stays unless content-identical in every class AND the move is parity-safe — the honest negative otherwise).
approach: CHARACTERIZATION + ORACLE, zero product change. (1) The capture map, both products: RUST (tip e2ee82f2d->b5bf28f1d during recon) captures HarnessDigestInputs at compact ENTER (session_engine/mod.rs:504 harness_digest_inputs: HarnessDigestContext flags [session-static] + digest_query_terms[persisted goal objective, last-4 user/assistant texts from the LIVE agent context] + NO disk read) and renders at the commit (compact_session.rs:437 render_with_fingerprint: fresh merged-harness-state disk read + the ENTER-captured terms -> the row's harnessDigest + harnessStateFingerprint); TS computes everything at the commit (agent-session.ts:8951 _harnessDigestWithFingerprint: live tool flags + fresh disk state + live goal + live-context last-4, right before appendCompaction). Placement-dependent surface = the terms (live-context texts + goal); the disk read happens at the same commit render point in both. (2) The class map over the divergence window (ENTER->commit: cut, tokens, details/aux, the summarizer wire calls, abort re-check): FROZEN everywhere EXCEPT the manual worker /compact command — TS freezes its whole window (isCompacting spans _performCompaction; _isBusyForSessionInput('pump') defers the input pump on it, agent-session.ts:7098), so TS's commit capture never sees mid-window rows; the Rust turn runner gate (worker/turn.rs:51) checks only input_pauses||queued_input_suspended — NO compacting term — and the designed resume sites (steer/follow_up commands, prompt-with-streamingBehavior, worker/input.rs:48-62 + handle_queue) clear the suspension MID-COMPACTION, so a racing turn starts DURING the compaction and lands its user row on the live context (prompt_with_images -> agent.prompt; no session-manager lock needed when digest_pending=false — the AgentSession's session-manager mutex is held across execute_compaction but the racing admission never takes it before the push). Auto-compaction (run_auto_compaction), the overflow arm, and the ACP arms hold the engine session lock across the window (frozen); the goal is frozen in every window (all goal mutations serialize on the session-manager lock the compaction holds). (3) THE ORACLES (in-tree, test-only, harness_digest.rs tests): Oracle A compact_digest_capture_placements_match_byte_for_byte_in_frozen_windows — the product's own ENTER capture vs a commit-moment capture sampled mid-window (the same pieces, no session lock; the goal pre-read with the freeze asserted post-window), asserting byte-identical rendered digests and the durable row carrying exactly that render, plus the state fingerprint placement-independence; served-path = the faux Delayed summarizer holds the request in flight (registration.call_count>=1) with the compact task unfinished at the sample. Oracle B compact_digest_capture_commit_time_placement_sees_racing_rows_enter_never_does — the racing admission's writer effect reproduced mid-window (the user row landing on the live context, the shape a resume-site turn produces), asserting the commit-moment capture sees the racing row (zebra terms), the two placements' rendered digests DIVERGE (the ranking flip: the zebra-bearing memory first at the commit-moment capture, the zero-term key order at ENTER), and THE SHIELD — the durable row keeps the ENTER (TS-frozen) content while the fingerprints match (the divergence is terms-driven ranking only).
parity_notes: THE PLACEMENT IS THE PORT'S TS-PARITY SHIELD, and it stays: the ENTER capture is strictly earlier than TS's commit capture, and TS's window is always writer-frozen, so the ENTER capture matches TS's effective commit-time content in EVERY class (frozen and racing alike). The record's deferral candidate is NOT parity-safe in the port as-is: in the racing class a commit-time capture would rank rows TS never sees (the runner-gap class), changing the frozen compaction content (the row's harnessDigest bytes). The deferral also has a second-order implementation hazard it would have to resolve first: a capture inside execute_compaction cannot take the session-manager lock (held across the window) — the goal read would have to move onto the already-borrowed &mut SessionManager. Frozen surfaces untouched: no product change; the compaction row, wire shapes, replay, and TUI bytes all identical; the oracle is test-only.
